subject: Approval request: one-time packaging credit + contract carveout for MedIngest
messages:
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: one-time packaging credit + contract carveout for MedIngest

Hi team,

Summary: MedIngest (prospect moving to POC) asked for a one-time packaging credit on our connector bundle plus a narrow contract carveout around third-party connector audits. They want this to close on a PO by next week. I need executive/finance/legal sign-off before I confirm.

What they asked for (verbatim):
- 40% "packaging" credit on connector fees for first 12 months
- Remove the vendor audit clause for partner-managed connectors (they claim SOC will not surface connector configs)
- 12-month committed term; they prefer quarterly invoicing

Commercial trade: we can push for 12M commit + milestone-based billing; the ask is material. Attached is a pricing matrix and a draft SOW showing the proposed scoping.

Preliminary impact (sales estimate): ~ $92k revenue concession in Y1 at list rates, but locks a $350k ARR account long-term.

Decision requested:
1) Approve up to what percent one-time packaging credit (I recommend max 30%).
2) Finance approval of accounting treatment and any cap ($ amount) we should enforce.
3) Legal guidance on acceptable audit carveouts (if any).

If the credit exceeds the approved amount we will need CFO sign-off (Marissa, please advise threshold). I can hold the commitment until I get a definitive answer — MedIngest has indicated they may sign before EOD Friday.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx, SOW-medingest-draft.pdf

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
pri yom_das@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: one-time packaging credit + contract carveout for MedIngest

Thanks for the write-up, Priyom.

High level: I’m comfortable with a one-time packaging credit to close this given the strategic upside, but we need guardrails. My provisional approval: up to 30% packaging credit, capped at $75k total concession, conditional on a 12-month committed term and milestone-linked invoicing. If MedIngest pushes beyond 30% or the $75k cap, this must go to CFO for explicit approval.

On the audit carveout: I don’t want to broadly remove our right to audit. Legal, can we limit scope instead — e.g., restrict audit to Redwood-managed infrastructure and exclude third-party connector maintenance activities? If Legal can draft narrow language that protects our visibility into data flows, I’m OK.

Finance (Marcus) — confirm how we should treat the concession in revenue (contra vs. credit memo) and whether $75k is an appropriate cap from an ARR/booking standpoint.

Priyom — hold off on any firm commitment until Marcus confirms the accounting treatment and we have a finalized SOW showing milestone payments. If MedIngest needs a doc to sign now, we can send the SOW with a placeholder note: "subject to executive approval."

-Marissa
Marissa Cole | VP, Commercials & GTM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Agree with Marissa's guardrails. Quick finance read:
- Approve up to 30% packaging credit, cap $75,000 (total concession).
- Accounting treatment: record as contra-revenue and allocate recognition over the first 6 months of the committed term; we will not backdate to ARR. Recommend using a one-time credit memo applied over the first two invoices — operationally easiest for the customer and for us.
- Require milestone-linked SOW and payment schedule; revenue recognition should align to milestones where possible.
- Regarding the legal carveout: we cannot remove our audit rights entirely. Legal can accept narrowing the audit scope to exclude vendor-only maintenance activities and specify that any audit request must be mutually agreed in advance and limited to access necessary to verify Redwood’s obligations.

I ran a quick sensitivity (attached finance-impact-medingest.csv). Under the approved cap, estimated P&L hit is manageable and the deal retains positive NPV at our targets.

If the customer pushes for a higher concession or asks for changes that alter cashflow materially (prepay vs. quarterly), escalate to CFO. Otherwise, Priyom has the green light to commit terms consistent with the above and to send the SOW for signature.

Marcus Lin | Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Chris — thanks for the conversation earlier. Following internal review, here’s what we can offer and the conditions to move to PO/SOW signature: 

Offer (final, exec-approved constraints):
- One-time packaging credit of 30% on connector bundle fees, capped at $75,000 total.
- Requires a 12-month committed term (minimum) and milestone-linked payments as described in the attached SOW.
- Legal carveout: we cannot fully remove our right to audit. We will narrow the scope so audits exclude routine third-party partner maintenance activities; any audit must be mutually agreed and limited to verifying Redwood’s obligations, not partner internal configs. Legal team will include precise clause language in the SOW.

Deliverables for signature:
- Attached: SOW-medingest-draft.pdf (contains milestone schedule and payment terms)
- We will generate a DocuSign envelope with the SOW and the commercial term addendum once you confirm acceptance. Link to DocuSign will follow: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/medingest-sow-4631

Conditions to close: acceptance of the cap and 12-month commit, and agreement to milestone billing. If you require different billing cadence or a higher concession we will need to escalate to our CFO for approval which will add time.

Please confirm by EOD Monday if you want us to proceed with DocuSign.
